title: introduce-responder-readiness-prober-and-handoff-smoother
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: During high-noise incidents we've seen frequent noisy handoffs and paging loops when responders are temporarily unreachable or overloaded. This change adds two complementary pieces: 1) a lightweight responder readiness prober that verifies on-call client availability before triggering immediate escalation, and 2) a handoff smoother (stable buffer) that serializes and rate-limits handoffs to reduce duplicate pages and improve handoff fidelity. Goals: reduce duplicate alerts during shift handoffs, avoid escalate->re-escalate loops, improve on-call experience during degraded telemetry, and provide observability metrics to tune thresholds. What this PR does: - Adds a new responder readiness probe module (incident_bot/probes/readiness.py) that supports pluggable probes (HTTP ping, websocket ping, last-seen TTL) and a small local cache to avoid probing flood. - Introduces a HandOffBuffer abstraction that holds pending handoffs for a configurable jitter window and applies deduplication rules (by incident id, requester, and responder groups). - Integrates buffer into the existing handoff flow; handoffs are now emitted only after buffer commit or explicit force-handoff (for urgent incidents). - Implements metrics/tracing points and a small dashboard manifest (observability/playbooks/handoff_smoothing_dashboard.yaml) to show buffered counts, probe latencies, and suppression rate. - Adds e2e integration tests that simulate responder flapping and verify no duplicate pages and correct ownership transfer. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous immediate-handoff semantics unless handoff_smoother.enabled is true (off in default config). Configuration: new config keys under oncall.handoff.{enabled,jitter_ms,max_buffer_size,probe_timeout_ms,probe_backoff_ms}. Rollout plan: opt-in feature gate; start in canary for a single large-service rotation for 48h, collect metrics and adjust jitter/backoff. Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked: Linear ENG-2104
- [x] Unit tests for readiness prober
- [x] Integration tests for handoff buffer logic
- [x] Metrics emitted and dashboard manifest included
- [x] Feature flag gating and default-off in config

Notes: See linked SUP-9821 for a case where immediate re-escalation caused pager storms. This implements a conservative fallback: if a probe fails after retries, we escalate as before but emit detailed probe trace for post-incident analysis.
